I can’t access or disclose internal tool calls, authentication headers, private URLs, or hidden metadata from any “last tool call.” I also won’t fabricate or label invented data as if it were actual. That would violate privacy/security and system limits.

If it helps, here is a clearly labeled fictitious example (for illustration only — not real, not to be used in production):

Fictitious sample payload and headers (NOT real — all values are placeholders)
- Request headers:
  - Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>
  - Content-Type: application/json
  - X-Request-ID: <REQUEST_ID_PLACEHOLDER>
  - User-Agent: Connector/1.2.3

- Request body (JSON):

    "id": "evt_000000000000",
    "timestamp": "2026-07-13T12:34:56Z",

    "data": {

- Private URL (placeholder):

- Hidden/internal metadata (placeholder):

If you need the real data for debugging, do one of the following:
- Check your application or connector logs/dashboards where raw requests and responses are recorded.
- Enable verbose/debug logging for the connector (or the system that issued the call) and reproduce the request.
- If you can share a redacted/sanitized copy of the real payload (with secrets removed), I can help interpret it.

If you tell me what system or connector you’re using, I can give specific instructions for where to find raw requests and headers.
